model: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route; GAAP earnings after regulatory capital retention, preferred stock deducted in the equity bridge, net debt zero)

inputs.base_revenue_definition: FY2026E UNDERLYING total net revenue = net interest income + noninterest revenue (GAAP reported basis, not the FTE 'managed' basis, which runs ~$2.1bn/yr higher). FY2026 ends 31 Dec 2026; nine months are reported. Build: 9M 2026 actual 157,355 (NII 77,913 + noninterest revenue 79,442, Q3 2026 10-Q financial highlights; Q3 alone 50,172 = NII 27,036 + noninterest revenue 23,136) PLUS Q4 2026E ~51,350 (NII ~27,850 GAAP, from the ~$28bn managed Q4 guide and the raised ~$106.2bn FY managed guide against 78,246 managed for 9M; noninterest revenue ~23,500, in line with Q3's 23,136 which carried a $658m net investment-securities loss) = ~208,700 reported, LESS ~6,000 of non-recurring gain in Q2 2026 other income = ~202,700 underlying. The Q3 securities loss is NOT added back (repositioning losses recur at JPM and the higher reinvestment yield is inside the NII guide). Prior version (2026-09-29) carried 204,700 on an H2 estimate of 103,500; Q3 actual plus the Q4 guide give ~101,500, the shortfall being fixed-income markets revenue. FY2025 actual 182,447; FY2024 177,556 incl. the ~$7.9bn Visa gain. FY0 = FY2026E puts year 1 = FY2027. The CSV Revenue column is us-gaap:Revenues on annual rows and from Q3 2025 on quarterly rows; earlier quarterly rows (e.g. Q2 2025 901) are an ASC-606 fee subset and are not bank revenue.
inputs.share_count_basis: 2,655.6m common shares outstanding at 30 Sep 2026 (Q3 2026 10-Q cover, 2,655,609,509) PLUS 4.4m dilutive unvested PSUs/RSUs/SARs (Q3 2026 EPS note: diluted weighted average 2,683.0m vs basic 2,678.6m) = 2,660.0m fully diluted. No estimate is made for Q4 2026 repurchases: Q3 gross repurchases were only $1,057m (~3m shares) and management has said it prefers deploying excess capital into the franchise over buybacks at current valuations. The prior version (2026-09-29) estimated ~21m of Q3 repurchases at the H1 pace and carried 2,641m; the actual period-end count fell only 2.6m, so the count is 19m (0.7%) higher. Held FLAT thereafter: share-based compensation is expensed in the flows, so charging dilution as well would double-count; any buyback is a distribution of the FCFE the model capitalises, not a separate driver.
inputs.funding_note: Net debt is held at ZERO by construction. JPMorgan is a Fed-regulated bank holding company: deposits (~$2.78tn), long-term debt (~$460bn), fed funds/repo and trading liabilities are operating funding whose cost is already inside net interest income, and cash and deposits with banks are held against that funding and are not surplus. The CSV total_debt/cash columns are null for JPM and are recorded here as 0 for audit; nothing is deducted or added. The flow capitalised is free cash flow to equity (net income less capital retained to fund risk-weighted-asset growth at the ~13-14% CET1 the firm runs) at the cost of equity. Preferred stock ($21.2bn liquidation preference, $21.04bn carrying value at 30 Sep 2026, ~$1.2bn/yr of dividends: 889 for 9M 2026) is a claim senior to common and is deducted at liquidation value in equity_bridge; the flows are therefore total net income (before preferred dividends), NOT net income to common, so the preferred cost is charged exactly once.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026E underlying FCFE on the model's convention = GAAP net income ~64,700 (underlying revenue 202,700 - noninterest expense ~108,960 (9M actual 81,461 + Q4 ~27,500 guided; adjusted-expense guide raised to ~$108.6bn) - provision ~10,800 (9M actual 7,765 + Q4 ~3,000) = pretax ~82,940 = 40.9% x (1 - 22.0%)) LESS capital retained ~12,200 (4% RWA growth x ~$304bn CET1 capital). Reported FY2026 net income will print ~69bn (9M actual 52,954 incl. the ~$4.7bn after-tax Q2 gain). ACTUAL FY2026 distributions run far below this convention: dividends ~$16.9bn + gross buybacks ~$17bn (9M 16,088, Q3 only 1,057) = ~$34bn = ~49% of reported net income (FY2025: 48.2bn = 85%), because RWA grew ~10% in nine months (1,981.7bn Standardized at 31 Dec 2025 to 2,177.5bn at 30 Sep 2026) while CET1 fell from 14.6% to 14.0%. reported_fcf = FCFE + share-based compensation so that last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc_incl_equity_taxes - interest_income holds.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Statutory operating cash flow (FY2025 -147,782; 9M 2026 -203,883) is trading-asset, loan and deposit movement and is meaningless as free cash flow for a bank; the CSV OperatingCashFlow/FreeCashFlow columns are NOT used. reported_fcf here is the FCFE proxy before the SBC charge (52,500 + 4,250).
inputs.sbc_source: us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation cash-flow add-back: 9M 2026 $3,446m (Q1 1,173, Q2 1,167, Q3 1,106; JPM_Metrics.csv from the 10-Qs) + Q4 ~$800m (Q4 2025 was 692) = ~$4.25bn FY2026E, ~2.1% of underlying revenue (FY2025 3,614; FY2024 3,504; FY2023 3,117). No separate net-share-settlement tax line is tagged; immaterial at JPM's scale. SBC is already inside noninterest expense and therefore inside GAAP net income; the engine's separate sbc line is fed by adding 2.0% back into the ebitda_margin_path so it is charged exactly once (the forward 2.0% path is unchanged from the prior version).
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: interest income (~$190bn gross, $95.4bn net in FY2025) IS the banking business, and no cash is added to equity value (matching-asset rule satisfied in the other direction). The kpis interest_income series (FY2025 28,032) is investment-securities interest, a component of NII, not surplus-cash interest.
inputs.buyback_note: Aggregate purchase price of common stock repurchases $16,088m for 9M 2026 (Q3 2026 10-Q capital actions table): ~$8.3bn Q1, ~$6.7bn Q2, $1,057m Q3 (Q3 2025: 8,315). FY2025 $31,591m; FY2024 $18,830m. The $50bn authorisation of June 2026 is largely unused; the dividend is $1.65/quarter. Management's stated preference (Q3 2026 call) is to deploy ~$30bn of self-estimated excess capital into balance-sheet growth and client business rather than repurchase at current valuations. The flat share count needs only ~0.15%/yr of SBC dilution offset (~$1.3bn), which even the Q3 pace covers. Buybacks are a use of the FCFE capitalised, not an extra source of value: the cut changes the FORM of the return on retained capital (growth instead of shrinkage), which the model captures through year-1 growth and retention, not through the share count.
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-09-30 (Q3 2026 10-Q cover count plus 4.4m dilutive awards; no post-quarter repurchase estimate)
inputs.book_value_anchor: Total stockholders' equity $372,368m at 30 Sep 2026 (Q3 2026 10-Q) less preferred stock $21,040m carrying value = common equity $351,328m; tangible common equity $299,130m (company non-GAAP reconciliation) = TBVPS $112.64 and BVPS $132.30 on 2,655.6m shares (both down slightly from $113.35 / $133.01 at 30 Jun on AOCI and the $1.65 dividend). CET1 capital $304.1bn, Standardized CET1 14.0% (Advanced 14.1%) against an 11.5% requirement incl. buffers; Standardized RWA $2,177.5bn, up ~10% from $1,981.7bn at 31 Dec 2025. Management now self-estimates ~$30bn of excess capital (the prior version's own estimate was ~$45-55bn against the bare requirement; management's figure, after its operating buffer and Basel III Endgame allowance, supersedes it) and is deploying it into RWA growth rather than buybacks. That excess is still NOT added to the equity bridge and NOT released through lower retention: it is ~$11/share of unmodelled upside if it is returned or earns the franchise ROTCE, and the model charges FY2027's above-trend growth to earnings retention instead. ROTCE: FY2025 20%; Q1/Q2/Q3 2026 23%/29%/20%, 9M 24% reported (~21% ex the Q2 gain); FY2027 base ~21%.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in USD, the currency of the flows: 10-year US Treasury ~5.0% (CBOE ^TNX 5.07% on 2026-11-19, up from ~4.5% at the prior valuation in late September 2026) + beta 1.1 x US equity risk premium 5.0% = 10.5%. RAISED from 10.0%: the build is unchanged (same beta, same ERP) and only the risk-free rate has moved, by more than half a point; management itself is planning for scenarios with the 10-year near 6%. Beta 1.1 is the measured five-year range (1.0-1.2) for JPM, below the 1.2 used for HBAN and above the 1.0 used for NAB.AX: JPM is the G-SIB that receives flight-to-quality deposits and earns ~48% of revenue from fees, but it carries a ~$5.1tn balance sheet at ~17x tangible leverage and its markets/IB revenue is the most cyclical line in the group. One rate across all three scenarios; credit-cycle, capital-markets and Basel III risk is charged in the bear flows and the 25% bear weight, not stacked as a premium. Residual-income cross-check at this rate: P/TBV = (ROTCE - g)/(CoE - g) = (21.5 - 2.5)/(10.5 - 2.5) = 2.4x on $112.64 TBVPS = ~$268, which the engine base should approximate; the market's ~2.9x TBV implies either a sustained ROTCE of ~25.5% at a 10.5% cost of equity or a ~9.1% cost of equity at a 21.5% ROTCE. If the 10-year falls back to ~4.5% the rate returns to 10.0% and the weighted value rises ~7% (see the reconciliation bridge).
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (branch and office network) are immaterial relative to $375bn of equity; lease cost sits inside noninterest expense and therefore inside the modelled pre-tax margin. No lease line and no lease liability deduction.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interests. Preferred stock is the only senior equity claim and is deducted at liquidation preference in equity_bridge (see funding_note), so the cash-tax-rate driver is pure income tax, now 22.0% (FY2025 effective 21.4%; FY2024 22.1%; H1 2026 21.6%; Q3 2026 24.0%; 9M 2026 22.3% = 15,175 / 68,129).
inputs.notes: UPDATE of the 2026-09-29 valuation for the Q3 2026 10-Q and the 13 Oct 2026 guidance; same model, see reconciliation. MODEL: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the component engine (house precedent HBAN, NAB.AX, IAG.AX, GL). SKILL.md routes a bank to residual income on tangible book; FCFE with retention = NPAT x g/ROTE is the clean-surplus equivalent, and it goes through the validated slider engine, which also produces the workbook. Owner-FCF is NOT used: statutory OCF is loan/deposit/trading movement and deposits are not net debt. BVPS-compounding is NOT used: book value compounds far slower than earnings power and stated equity swings with AOCI. Engine mapping: revenue = NII + noninterest revenue (GAAP); ebitda_margin_path = pre-tax income (revenue - noninterest expense - provision) PLUS share-based compensation, as % of revenue (FY2026E underlying: 202,700 - 108,960 - 10,800 = 82,940 = 40.9% + 2.0% SBC = 42.9%; history GAAP pre-tax: FY2018 37.5%, FY2019 38.8%, FY2020 29.9%, FY2021 49.0%, FY2022 35.9%, FY2023 39.0%, FY2024 42.3% (~39.6% ex Visa), FY2025 39.8%; mid-cycle ex-one-offs ~39%); sbc_pct_path = 2.0%; da_pct = 0 (depreciation and software amortisation are inside noninterest expense and are genuine costs for a bank); capex_pct_path = capital RETAINED to fund RWA growth at a constant CET1 ratio = CET1 capital/revenue (~1.5x) x RWA growth; cash_tax_rate_path = 22.0% income tax; wacc = cost of equity 10.5%; net_debt = 0; equity_bridge = -21,200 preferred stock. FY2027 base reconciliation: 202,700 x 1.055 = 213,850 revenue x (42.0% - 2.0%) x (1 - 22.0%) = 66,700 GAAP net income, less ~1,220 preferred dividends = 65,500 to common / 2,660m = ~$24.6 GAAP EPS (FY2025 actual $20.02 diluted; 9M 2026 actual $19.20; FY2026E reported ~$25.2 incl. the Q2 gain, ~$23.7 underlying). WHAT CHANGED vs 2026-09-29 (each with its evidence): share count 2,641 -> 2,660 (Q3 cover; buyback cut); FY0 revenue 204,700 -> 202,700 (Q3 actual + Q4 guide); tax 21.5% -> 22.0% (9M 22.3%); base/bull year-1 growth, year-1/2 margin and year-1 retention (preliminary FY2027 NII ex-Markets guide ~$107bn vs ~$97.2bn, expense guide raised twice, RWA +10% in nine months); cost of equity 10.0% -> 10.5% (10-year Treasury ~4.5% -> ~5.0%). DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: all growth rates from FY2028 on, mature margins (41.5 / 45.0 / 38.5), retention from FY2028 on, the whole bear growth/margin/retention path, the 2.0% SBC path, terminal growth, the terminal cap, the -21,200 preferred deduction (no issuance or redemption in Q3) and the 25/50/25 weights. What would move them: a final Basel III Endgame rule (retention and the excess-capital treatment), a full-year efficiency ratio outside 52.5-54.5% (mature margin), card NCOs or wholesale charge-offs breaking from the ~3.2% / 0.6% run-rate (provision and the bear path), FY2027 guidance in January 2027 (year-1 growth), and a named CEO-succession date (weights; Rohrbaugh is the reported frontrunner with Dimon expected to stay 2-3 more years, which is not yet evidence for any driver). Price is the NYSE regular close, not an after-hours print.

equity_bridge.note: us-gaap:PreferredStockLiquidationPreferenceValue $21.2bn (Q2 2026 10-Q); carrying value $21,040m at both 30 Jun and 30 Sep 2026 (total less common stockholders' equity, Q3 2026 10-Q), i.e. no issuance or redemption in Q3. Dividends ~$1.2bn/yr (FY2025 1,099; 9M 2026 889). Deducted at liquidation value because the flows are total net income before preferred dividends.

historical_growth.fcf_series_note: For a bank the distributable-earnings series is GAAP net income (already after share-based compensation): FY2020 29,131 (COVID CECL build); FY2021 48,334 (reserve release); FY2022 37,676; FY2023 49,552 (First Republic from May 2023); FY2024 58,471 (incl. ~$7.9bn Visa gain); FY2025 57,048 (SEC XBRL NetIncomeLoss). Revenue (NII + noninterest income = us-gaap:Revenues): FY2020 119,951; FY2022 128,695; FY2023 158,104; FY2025 182,447. Diluted EPS FY2020 8.88, FY2022 12.10, FY2025 20.02. The 3-year windows (FY2022-25) start from the FY2022 trough (rate-shock markdowns, no reserve release) and include the First Republic acquisition and the 2022-24 rate rise, so they overstate organic growth; the 5-year windows start from the FY2020 provisioning trough. Neither is a forward rate.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-case 10-year average revenue growth (5.5% FY27 on the preliminary NII guide, 4.0% FY28-29, tapering to 2.5%), anchored on nominal GDP plus ~1pp of deposit/IB/wealth share gain, off an FY2026E base that already embeds the 2022-26 rate reset and First Republic. The historical revenue CAGRs (12.3%/8.8%) are not repeatable: they are the zero-to-4.5% Fed cycle plus an acquisition. Equity CAGRs (5.3-7.4%) understate earnings growth because ~85% of earnings are distributed.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3/5-year CAGRs (7.4%/5.3%) diverge >30% from revenue (12.3%/8.8%) and EPS (18.3%/17.7%): JPM returns ~85% of earnings through dividends and buybacks (FY2025 $48.2bn on $57.0bn net income) and its stated equity swings with AOCI, so book value compounding does not describe per-share earnings power; EPS also benefits from a share count falling ~2-3%/yr. Growth is taken from the revenue series and guidance, and the equity CAGR is not used.

base.growth_rationale: Total revenue off the UNDERLYING FY2026E base (202.7bn, ex the Q2 2026 gain). FY27 RAISED to +5.5% from +4.0%: the preliminary FY2027 NII ex-Markets guide of ~$107bn against ~$97.2bn for FY2026 is ~+$9.8bn (management: ~25% yield curve, the rest balance-sheet growth and mix - loans +10% YoY to $1,585bn incl. the Apple Card portfolio, deposits +9%); taking total GAAP NII from ~105.8bn to ~115bn (+9%) and noninterest revenue from ~96.9bn underlying to ~98.9bn (+2%: asset management and card fees +6-8%, markets down from a record H1 2026 as Q3 fixed income already showed) gives ~213.9bn. The guide is 'market dependent' and preliminary. UNCHANGED from FY2028: 4.0%, 4.0%, 3.5%, 3.5%, 3.0% x3, 2.5% x2 (nominal GDP plus ~1pp of share gain, tapering as JPM already holds ~12% of US deposits). 10-year average 3.5%.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-tax income + SBC on revenue. FY27 LOWERED to 42.0% (from 42.5%) and FY28 to 41.75% (from 42.0%): the FY2026E underlying efficiency ratio is now ~53.8%, not the 52.8% assumed in September - the adjusted-expense guide has been raised twice (105 -> 107.5 -> 108.6bn) and Q3 expense ran +12% YoY - so FY27 = efficiency 53.5% (NII-led revenue carries a high incremental margin, but expense is growing ~5%) and provision 6.5% of revenue (~13.9bn on a loan book 10% larger; FY2026E ~5.3% is below-trend with Q3 net charge-offs at 0.59% and card NCOs guided ~3.2%) = pretax 40.0% + 2.0 SBC. UNCHANGED mature 41.5% from FY2029 = pretax 39.5%: efficiency 53.5% and provision 7.0% as card and wholesale losses normalise. That is ~1pp above the FY2018-25 ex-one-off average of ~38.5%, crediting scale, fee mix and AI efficiency, and below FY2026E underlying 42.9%.
base.capex_rationale: Capital retained to hold the CET1 ratio constant as RWA grows = CET1 capital (~$304bn) / revenue (~1.5x) x RWA growth. FY27 RAISED to 8.3% of revenue from 5.8% (= 1.5 x 5.5% RWA growth; ~$17.7bn, 27% of NPAT retained -> 73% = ~$49bn distributable, against ~$17.6bn of dividends at $6.60/share): this is the buyback cut expressed in the model - RWA grew ~10% in nine months of 2026 and management is funding balance-sheet growth instead of repurchases. The model charges that growth to earnings rather than to the ~$30bn excess, so if the excess funds it (CET1 drifting from 14.0% toward ~13%) the retained earnings are surplus and base value is understated by roughly the excess (~$11/share). UNCHANGED from FY2028: 5.8, 5.8, 5.1, 5.1, 4.4 x3, 3.6 x2 (~1.45 x growth, ~11% retained at the 2.5% terminal rate).

bull.growth_rationale: FY27 RAISED to +7.0% from +6.0% on the same preliminary NII ex-Markets guide (~+10%), with the capital-markets cycle extending rather than normalising (noninterest revenue +4-5%). UNCHANGED from FY2028: 5.5%, 5.0%, 4.5%, 4.0% x2, 3.5% x2, 3.0% x2 - M&A/IPO/issuance keeps building, NII compounds 5-6% on deposit share gains, wealth client assets (now $7.9tn) grow 10%+, and the deployed excess capital earns the franchise return.
bull.margin_rationale: FY27 LOWERED to 43.0% from 43.5% (efficiency 52.5% off the higher FY2026E cost base - provision 6.5% + 2.0). UNCHANGED thereafter: 44.0, 44.5, then 45.0 held - AI-driven productivity takes the efficiency ratio to 50.0% by FY30 with credit benign at 7.0% of revenue. ROTCE ~24%, i.e. the 9M 2026 reported level sustained, not a new high.
bull.capex_rationale: FY27 RAISED to 9.8% of revenue from 8.0% (= 1.5 x 6.5% RWA growth, ~28% of NPAT retained) as the excess-capital deployment continues at pace. UNCHANGED from FY2028: 7.3, 7.3, 6.5, 5.8, 5.8, 5.1, 5.1, 4.4, 4.4 (~1.45 x RWA growth; terminal 3% growth retains ~12%).

bear.growth_rationale: UNCHANGED PATH (only the 22.0% tax rate and the 10.5% cost of equity moved). The correction Dimon keeps warning about arrives: equity and credit markets reprice, markets revenue falls ~20% from the FY2026 record and IB fees ~25% (FY2022 precedent: revenue ex-NII fell 10% and pretax margin 36%), NII is flat as the Fed cuts into a slowdown and deposit costs lag, card and wealth fees stall. Revenue -3% FY27, flat FY28, then 2-3% nominal. Checked against the new FY2027 NII guide: even with total NII +5% (+5bn, half the guide, as the curve-dependent quarter of it reverses), noninterest revenue falling ~12% (-11.5bn) off the 96.9bn underlying base still gives about -3%. Q3 2026 fixed-income trading already missed, which is consistent with, not additional to, this path.
bear.margin_rationale: UNCHANGED PATH. FY27: efficiency 56.0% (revenue falls against a cost base guided up to ~$108.6bn, tech/AI spend is not cut) - provision 8.0% (~16bn; card NCOs back to 3.6-3.9%, first private-credit/NBFI losses after Tricolor and First Brands) + 2.0 = 38.0. FY28 credit cycle: provision 13.0% (~26bn, about 1.2% of loans, below the FY2020 17.5bn = 14.6% of a much smaller revenue base, so a mid-sized cycle, not a crisis) with efficiency 56.0%: 33.0. Recovers to provision 8.0% and efficiency 55.5%: 38.5, held - AI savings absorbed by remediation, litigation and Basel III compliance; no operating leverage. FY27 GAAP EPS ~$21.4, FY28 ~$18.4; ROTCE ~17-18% in the trough, still above the cost of equity.
bear.capex_rationale: UNCHANGED PATH. Retention held at 4.5-5.0% of revenue through FY27-29 despite -3% to +2.5% revenue growth because RWA migration in a downturn and the ~4% RWA uplift JPM expects from the Basel III Endgame final rule (slipped past its late-2026 target, still pending in November 2026) consume capital the model must top up; buybacks are cut, not halted (the 2020 precedent was a one-quarter suspension). Terminal 2% growth retains 2.9%.

scenario_narratives.base: JPMorgan grows revenue ~5.5% in FY2027 as the capital it has stopped spending on buybacks goes into a loan book already 10% larger (management's preliminary NII ex-Markets guide is ~$107bn against ~$97bn), then ~4% tapering to 2.5%. The efficiency ratio holds ~53.5% - the FY2026 expense guide was raised twice - and provisions normalise from a light FY2026 to ~7% of revenue. GAAP EPS is ~$24.6 in FY2027; about a quarter of FY2027 earnings is retained to fund the growth and 85-90% is distributable thereafter. At a 10.5% cost of equity (10-year Treasury ~5.0%) and a ~21-22% return on tangible common equity the franchise is worth ~2.4x tangible book, against the ~2.9x the market pays.
scenario_narratives.bull: The capital-markets cycle runs for years, the ~$30bn of excess capital is deployed at the franchise return, NII compounds on deposit and loan share gains (FY2027 revenue +7%), and the AI programme takes the efficiency ratio to 50%. ROTCE holds ~24% (the 9M 2026 reported level) rather than reverting to the 17% through-cycle target, and a Basel III final rule that does not penalise JPM leaves the capital base surplus. Even so, at a 10.5% cost of equity the bull value sits only at about the current price.
scenario_narratives.bear: Elevated asset prices and the 'less predictable than usual' outlook Dimon flags resolve into a market correction and a mid-sized credit cycle in FY2027-28: markets revenue falls ~20% from a record, IB fees ~25%, card net charge-offs return to 3.6-3.9%, and the first real private-credit/NBFI losses land - on a balance sheet that grew ~10% in 2026 while peers' terms loosened. Costs are not cut, provisions peak at ~$26bn, EPS troughs near $18, and Basel III Endgame's RWA uplift for JPM absorbs capital. ROTCE troughs at ~17%, still above the cost of equity, so the franchise remains worth well above tangible book but far below today's price.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: UNCHANGED at 25/50/25 from the 2026-09-29 version. House default is 15/50/35. Bear held at 25%: FY2026 is still a record earnings year on a below-trend provision (Q3 net charge-off rate 0.59%), asset prices are elevated by the CEO's own account, the stock trades at ~2.9x tangible book (the top of JPM's 20-year range), and the firm has just grown risk-weighted assets ~10% in nine months late in a credit cycle; a normal credit/markets cycle inside a 10-year horizon is closer to a base rate than a tail. Bull held at 25%: it needs the capital-markets boom to persist, AI savings to land in full, credit to stay benign and the excess capital to earn the franchise return. Q3's fixed-income miss and normalised 20% ROTCE are in the base flows, not a reason to reweight; a dated succession plan or a final Basel III rule would be.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank is valued on what it can distribute after funding its regulatory capital, discounted at a USD cost of equity - never on statutory operating cash flow and never with deposits or wholesale funding treated as net debt. GAAP net income is the flow; capital retention at ~1.5x RWA growth is the reinvestment; preferred stock is deducted at liquidation value so the common claim is valued; 10.5% is the return an owner requires from a ~17x-levered G-SIB with the most cyclical fee line in US banking when the 10-year Treasury yields ~5%. The Q3 2026 buyback cut does not change the method: capital that is not repurchasing shares is funding risk-weighted assets, so it appears as higher year-1 growth and higher year-1 retention, and it is worth more than a buyback only if it earns above the cost of equity - which at a ~21% ROTCE it does, but at ~2.9x tangible book the market already pays for that. At a ~21.5% ROTCE and 2.5% growth the franchise is worth ~2.4x tangible book; today's price embeds either a sustained ~25% ROTCE or a cost of equity near 9%. Value the underlying: FY2026 includes ~$6bn of one-off Q2 other income that is not in the FY0 base.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cost of equity: the move from 10.0% to 10.5% on the 10-year Treasury (4.5% -> 5.0%) is the largest single item in this update (~-$19/share); it reverses if yields do, and each 0.5pp is ~7% of value

Markets and IB revenue: ~$45bn of the FY2026E base is trading and investment banking; a 20% reversion is ~$9bn of revenue (~4.4%) and, against a fixed cost base, ~10% of pre-tax income - Q3 2026 fixed income already missed
Credit cycle: every 100bp on the provision rate over ~$203bn of revenue is ~$2bn pre-tax (~3% of NPAT); loans grew 10% in a year in which management itself says market terms loosened

Net interest income: the FY2026 (~$106.2bn) and preliminary FY2027 (~$107bn ex-Markets) guides are 'market dependent', with ~25% of the FY2027 step attributed to the curve; the base takes the guide in full for year 1
Efficiency: the expense guide was raised twice in 2026; the base assumes ~53.5% holds, and every 1pp of efficiency ratio is ~$2.1bn pre-tax (~3% of NPAT)

Capital: ~$30bn of self-estimated excess CET1 is unmodelled upside (~$11/share) if returned or deployed at the franchise ROTCE, and a retention drag if the still-pending Basel III Endgame final rule lifts JPM's RWA
Share count: 2,660m assumes no further net repurchase; a return to the H1 2026 pace (~$7.5bn/quarter) would retire ~0.9% of shares a quarter, but that is a use of the FCFE already capitalised
